query: We want our own implementation of this vendor library, but legal says we cannot have anyone who read their source write our version. How do we structure that?
The license on the original is incompatible with ours. I need a functionally equivalent replacement built without borrowing any of their code.
This PHP billing engine is 12k lines of spaghetti nobody understands. I want to throw it away and build a fresh one that behaves identically.
Rather than untangle this parser, I'd like to start over on a blank file and reproduce its behavior exactly — nothing copied across.
Plan is: one agent documents everything the old service does, then a second agent builds the new one from that document alone, never seeing the old code. Help me run that.
Can we split this into a spec phase and a build phase, where the builder only gets the written behavior description and no snippets?
I want to port this Java tool to Go, but by writing down what it does first and implementing from that, not by translating it line by line.
Write me a behavioral specification of this module complete enough that someone could rebuild it from scratch without ever opening the original.
This module has no tests and I'm scared to touch it. Help me pin down what it currently does before I change anything.
I need to add a feature to a 2000-line class with hidden database dependencies and no way to test locally. Where do I break the dependencies?
Extract these three nested conditionals into named methods and reduce the duplication, without changing behavior.
Clean up this file in place — rename the confusing variables, inline the pointless wrapper, move the helpers where they belong.
Rewrite this messy module, it's gotten ugly.
Let's incrementally strangle the old endpoint: keep it running while we route traffic to a new one, piece by piece.
Write characterization tests around this pricing function so I can safely refactor it afterwards.
Draft a spec and acceptance criteria for a brand new notification feature we haven't built yet.
Implement the CSV export endpoint with tests, test first.
Review the diff on this branch against our coding standards.
